question: Should Discord Activity support proceed as a hardened Canvas/Discord plugin-owned feature, be split into a smaller launch/deploy fix, or be paused in favor of another Activity branch?
rationale: The PR crosses plugin ownership, config compatibility, Gateway auth, credential transport, and availability boundaries; automation cannot choose the permanent security and product contract for Activity access.

options.title: Rework under plugin ownership
options.body: Port the feature to current `extensions/discord` and `extensions/canvas` seams, require a credentialed or signed Activity auth path, remove URL tokens, and add fanout limits before re-review.

options.title: Split the narrow Discord launch work
options.body: If only the launch-button or Entry Point behavior is urgent, land that as a smaller Discord plugin PR while leaving Activity bridge/auth design for a separate review.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep or close one of the overlapping Activity branches after maintainers choose the canonical direction, rather than carrying two dirty landing candidates.

recommendation.title: Rework under plugin ownership
recommendation.body: Port the feature to current `extensions/discord` and `extensions/canvas` seams, require a credentialed or signed Activity auth path, remove URL tokens, and add fanout limits before re-review.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-risk decision is the Canvas plugin/config/auth boundary, and recent history points to steipete for that area.
